'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Maria Cantwell]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Maria Cantwell]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsWA}} The '''2024 United States Senate election in Washington''' was held on November 5, 2024, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Washington (state)|Washington]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent Senator [[Maria Cantwell]] was elected to her fifth term, winning over [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] physician Raul Garcia. Cantwell improved on her prior [[2018 United States Senate election in Washington|2018 performance]] despite the Republican national environment. She won 59.09% of the vote, up from 58.43% in 2018 and marking a 1.6% leftward shift from that race. Washington had the smallest swing of any state in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Washington (state)|concurrent presidential race]], swinging rightward by under 1% from [[2020 United States presidential election in Washington (state)|2020]]. Cantwell slightly outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the concurrent [[2024 United States presidential election in Washington (state)|U.S. presidential election in Washington]], winning [[Pacific County, Washington|Pacific County]] which also voted for [[Donald Trump]]. Cantwell won by a margin of 18.45%, narrowly higher than Harris's 18.22% margin.{{toclimit|3}} Republicans have not won a Senate race in Washington since [[1994 United States Senate election in Washington|1994]]. ==Primary election== The blanket primary election was held on August 6, 2024.{{cite web |title=Primary elections in Washington, 2024
